countsMean.frames: The SWEEP's own count, not a total of what is committed: it is exactly the frames on disk that fall OUTSIDE every set declared under `supplementary`, which is the equality `check-evidence.mjs` asserts. What is on disk is this number plus the declared sets; the live accounting - disk total, per-set counts, and how a merge recomputes these rather than carrying either side's number - is recorded in `docs/evidence/chat-usage/README.md` under 'Evidence accounting after the merge'. A narrowed run preserves the previous value by construction, so after one, that section is where this number's currency is stated - a bare figure here went stale exactly that way once before.
countsMean.surfaces: `capture-evidence.mjs`'s `STORIES.length` at the head named above; the live value is this file's own `surfaces` field. `check-evidence.mjs` does not assert it, and a narrowed run carries the previous value over - which is how it went one round stale before this prose existed - so after anything but a full sweep, verify against the story list (or the README accounting section) before quoting it.

USAGE REVIEW ROUND 1: all twelve `chat-usage` story surfaces were RE-CAPTURED in both brand themes (24 frames) because the round changed what they show, not merely how they look. Two of them were the point: `loading` and `fetching` previously photographed states the shipped container could not produce (an ENABLED `Ask providers now` at first paint, when react-query reports isLoading and isFetching together; and cached numbers retained during a live ask, which the query key switch discarded). Both states are now reachable in the app, so both frames are captured from the real behaviour rather than from hand-fed props, and the agreement between story args and container props is pinned by scripts/usage-container.test.mjs rather than by this note. The other ten were re-captured because the fixes are visible in them: the bar track now carries a `border-control` boundary (measured 1.11:1 -> 2.05:1 against the card on the rendered dark frame, which is what makes a 0% row read as an empty meter and a 100% row as a full one), the unmeasurable window's dotted rule moved off floor-exempt `ink-disabled` onto `ink-dim`, staleness is measured against the set's newest confirmation so `stale-report` again shows one marked block beside one unmarked, prose left monospace, and the tally and the dead-grant note changed wording. `chat-usage--loading`'s capture viewport grew 360 -> 470 so the third skeleton block is not sliced through its own card border. `real-data/` was ALSO re-captured, from the same real backend response replayed through scripts/usage-real-evidence.mjs --payload, because it is the frame two of the fixes were diagnosed from: it read `Cached report, just now.` above blocks dated `1h ago` and showed all eleven blocks degraded. It now reads `Cached report, 34m ago.` and marks 10 of 11 - openrouter, the one account genuinely confirmed at the newest stamp, is unmarked - so the staleness mark distinguishes something again. USAGE REVIEW ROUND 2 (remediation): the same twelve `chat-usage` story surfaces were RE-CAPTURED in both brand themes (24 frames) because the scroll-fold treatment changed what most of them show. The fold rule is no longer an unconditional per-picker prop: it is measured per state from the scroll container, so the six states whose content ends above the fold (`empty`, `query-error`, `fetching`, `percent-only`, `remaining-balance`, `narrow`) no longer draw a boundary under nothing, and the states that do overflow carry a `border-control` rule (3:1 structural floor, pinned at the call site in scripts/contrast-contract.mjs) plus a 20px bottom fade that retracts at the end of the list. `loading` also changed copy: the first paint reads `Reading cached usage` rather than `Asking providers`, because opening the view is a cache read and not a provider ask. No story was added or deleted, so `frames` (498) and `surfaces` (57) are unchanged and still equal what is on disk. `real-data/` was NOT re-captured this round and is STALE with respect to the fold treatment: it still shows the round-1 clip. This machine's backend currently returns zero provider reports, so scripts/usage-real-evidence.mjs cannot re-derive the frame, and no saved `--payload` response from the 11-report run survives in the repository (it is deliberately never committed). The fold fix was instead verified at that exact density in the interaction harness - 11 provider blocks, 22 windows, 1217px of content in a 520px box - measuring a 1px `border-control` rule and a gradient mask at the top of the scroll and the mask retracted with the rule still present at the bottom, in both brand themes. Everything else `real-data` is evidence for (the staleness baseline, the description line, the multi-account keying) is unaffected by this round's changes. USAGE REVIEW ROUND 3: the story `chat-usage--dense` was ADDED (the thirteenth chat-usage surface, 2 frames in the two brand themes), so `frames` (498 -> 500) and `surfaces` (57 -> 58) were corrected by hand per the accounting rule above. It exists because the only committed frame at overflowing density was `real-data/`, which is one commit stale against the fold treatment and cannot be re-derived on demand; `dense` is the same density built from fixtures - eleven reports, twenty-eight windows, five anthropic accounts, the identities and labels the real response shapes - so any sweep can re-take it. The fold it photographs was measured in the same session against the same Storybook build, in both brand themes: 1273px of content in the 520px body cap (753px hidden), a 20px gradient mask plus a 1px `border-control` rule on the wrapper at scrollTop 0, the mask RETRACTED with the rule still present at scrollTop max, and no treatment at all on a fitting state (`percent-only` measured 0px hidden, no mask, 0px border). `real-data/` was NOT re-captured, and this time the live refill was attempted for real: the exact request the button makes (GET /v1/desktop/usage?live=true&refresh=true, authenticated with the running server's own desktop bearer) answered source=live with ZERO reports in ~50ms, and explicit per-provider asks for every usage-capable provider also returned zero - the backend's current credential view has no usage-reportable providers, so its cache cannot be refilled from here. `real-data/` therefore remains stale with respect to the fold treatment, its staleness stays recorded, and the fold at real density is evidenced by `dense`, which is re-derivable. The thirteen `chat-usage` story surfaces were RE-CAPTURED at the final rebased head 601a7eece (26 frames, both brand themes) because `capture-evidence.mjs` itself changed in the merge and #111 changed `src/main`, so `head`, `srcTree` and `scriptsTree` above name the commit these frames actually came from. All 26 reproduced BYTE-IDENTICALLY to the pre-rebase set the review rounds signed off, which is the measured evidence that neither #114 nor #111 changed anything this view renders and that the design sign-off still describes the pixels on the current head. One caveat recorded honestly: the first capture run at this head produced a `stale-report/localOperatorDark.webp` differing from the approved frame in 81 of 682,000 pixels (max channel delta 4/255) inside one 13x12 block, and a second run at the SAME head and the same Storybook build reproduced the approved bytes exactly - so that was nondeterministic encoder/raster noise at the threshold of the capture, not a rendering change; the committed frame is the byte-identical one. So the frames in this tree come from three heads, not one: `chat-usage/` story frames from the rebased head `a5e20c4bc` (taken at its pre-amend twin, per the provenance note above), `write-edit-diff/` from #114's own capture at 96171dac, and the older sweep frames from the August head as recorded above.

supplementary.why: The claims are a real pointer hover and a click that stages a draft. Storybook can force the revealed class but not produce the hover, and a staged draft is store state a fixture would have to fake, so these are captured from the running app against an isolated seeded backend instead. The sidebar has no story, so re-running the sweep cannot re-derive them; docs/evidence/sidebar-new-chat/README.md carries the re-capture procedure.

supplementary.source: headless Chrome over CDP, driven by `node scripts/diff-body-evidence.mjs`: the shipped `applyHistoryPage` reducer and the shipped `CanonicalTranscript` over a real durable history page read from one real session's `transcript.jsonl` in the local store (`--session` and `--anchor` are required arguments; the id is deliberately not committed)
supplementary.why: The story renders a TranscriptRecord this repository built, so it proves the component. This set starts one layer earlier, at the bytes `/v1/desktop/sessions/{id}/history` serves — the stored rows, serialised verbatim by `read_transcript_page` — and runs them through the shipped reducer, which is what proves the payload reaches pixels: the durable row's own encoding, the extraction of `provider_payload.details.diff`, the identity gate and the args-drop rule. It cannot be re-derived by the sweep, and the payload itself is deliberately NOT committed: the harness writes it to a temp file and deletes it. Re-run with `node scripts/diff-body-evidence.mjs --session=<id> --anchor=<row id>` (see docs/evidence/write-edit-diff/README.md).

The only frames in this tree rendered against a REAL /v1/desktop/usage response rather than story fixtures: 11 provider reports and 28 windows as the local backend actually returned them, which is what proves the ported view renders the wire shape and not merely its own fixtures. Storybook cannot produce them (the payload needs the desktop bearer), so the sweep cannot re-derive these two frames. Account identities are redacted shape-preservingly by the capture script; every number, window, tier, unit and staleness value is the backend's own. docs/evidence/chat-usage/README.md carries the re-capture procedure. RE-CAPTURED for review round 1 from the same real response (replayed via `--payload`, since this machine's backend now returns zero reports and cannot re-derive it): the committed pair was the evidence for the staleness-baseline and description defects, so leaving it would have shipped a picture of the bug beside its fix. ROUND 3: a genuine live refill was attempted (live=true&refresh=true with the server's own bearer, plus explicit per-provider asks) and the backend returned zero reports for every provider - its credential view currently has no usage-reportable providers - so these two frames remain one commit stale with respect to the round-2 fold treatment. The fold at this density is evidenced by the re-derivable `chat-usage--dense` story instead.
